_README: TEMPLATE ONLY - every address, datatype and scale below is a PLACEHOLDER.
Do not load this as-is. The values must come from the energy meter's own
Modbus register table in its manual. A plausible-looking guess is worse
than an empty map, because someone will trust the numbers it produces.
To use it:
1. create the meter model:
POST /api/admin/meter-models
{ "manufacturer": "...", "model": "...",
"defaultBaudRate": 9600, "defaultParity": "none",
"defaultStopBits": 1, "verified": true }
2. fill in every entry below from the manual, set meterModelId
3. POST the whole file to /api/admin/registers/bulk
4. assign the model to the meter and replay a stored packet from
/api/commissioning/raw/:id/replay to check the decode
FIELD NOTES
functionCode    3 = read holding registers, 4 = read input registers
registerAddress as printed in the manual. Watch for the 40001 vs 0
convention - some manuals list 40001 for address 0.
registerLength  16-bit registers the value spans (FLOAT32 = 2)
datatype        INT16 UINT16 INT32 UINT32 INT64 UINT64 FLOAT32
FLOAT64 BOOL BITFIELD
byteOrder       order of the two bytes inside one register
wordOrder       order of the registers inside a multi-register value
big/big       ABCD  (Modbus default)
big/little    CDAB  (word swapped - very common)
little/big    BADC  (byte swapped)
little/little DCBA
If decoded values look like nonsense but the right
order of magnitude, wordOrder is the first thing to flip.
scale/valueOffset  engineering value = raw * scale + valueOffset
sourceKey       the vendor's own JSON key, for when the GATEWAY decodes
the register and sends it by name instead of raw words
metricKey       must exist in the platform catalogue; see GET /api/admin/metrics

notes: PLACEHOLDER. This is the one to get right - it drives every kWh figure.
Check the manual for: the unit (Wh vs kWh - use scale 0.001 for Wh),
the register width, and the value the counter rolls over at. Add that
rollover ceiling to ENERGY_COUNTER_ROLLOVER_VALUES so a wrap is
credited instead of being read as a meter reset.
